items.question: How is an AI receptionist for cleaning companies different from an answering service?
items.answer: The difference is what happens after the greeting. Your agent asks the scope questions and checks your service area. It prices a standard clean and books the crew on your calendar, so the customer record exists in your booking software before the call ends.

items.question: What does the agent handle, and what still reaches a human?
items.answer: The agent handles intake, qualification, standard quoting, booking, reminders, and follow-up. It routes to a human on four triggers: a walk-through estimate, an urgent flag, a disputed charge, or a request outside the rules you set. Every handoff arrives with the full transcript attached.

items.question: How does it handle one-time deep cleans versus recurring customers?
items.answer: Both run the same intake, then split. A one-time scope gets a flat rate and the earliest slot that fits the crew. A recurring lead gets a cadence, a plan price, and payment on file, and the agent returns after the first visit to offer the second.

items.question: Does it work for our cleaning type, including commercial walk-throughs?
items.answer: Residential maid, commercial, janitorial, and vacation-rental turnover all follow the same qualify, quote, book, remind, follow-up sequence. Only the variables change. Commercial accounts that need a site visit get a walk-through booked instead of a price, with the square footage and access notes already captured.

items.question: What changes in our speed-to-lead and missed-call rate?
items.answer: Every inbound request gets a first response in under a minute, including nights and weekends, and every missed call gets a text back within seconds. Worth saying what this does not fix. If one person already answers every call inside working hours, your voicemail is fine and this will not pay for itself.

items.question: Who owns the customer data and the conversation records?
items.answer: You do. Call recordings, transcripts, photos, and customer records sit in your account, and Acme never uses them to train public AI models. Retention windows are yours to set. If you bring your own LLM API key, the AI calls stay inside your provider relationship.

items.question: How long does deployment take?
items.answer: Between 5 and 15 days for a lead-handling agent, depending on how many channels you switch on and how clean your booking data is. The template arrives built, so the work is connecting your stack, setting pricing rules, and listening to the first conversations.

items.question: How do credits map to call and message volume?
items.answer: Each agent action draws a set credit cost: a conversation turn, an availability lookup, a calendar write, a customer record update. A text-led month costs less than a voice-led one at the same lead volume, and a slow month costs less than a peak one. Nothing is billed per seat.

items.question: Can the platform extend beyond lead handling later?
items.answer: Yes. The same canvas and the same connected stack run cleaner recruiting, customer service on active jobs, supply ordering, and contract renewals. You add a flow rather than buying another tool. The platform view of the same agent sits on the conversational AI platform page.
